brief:
Nearly half of all terrorism arrests in Britain since the 9/11 attacks occurred after the government banned Palestine Action, a direct action group, according to new data reported by Middle East Eye. The proscription of the organization, which had conducted direct action campaigns against Israeli operations in the UK, coincided with a marked acceleration in counter-terrorism enforcement activity.

The concentration of arrests in the period following the ban raises significant questions about the scale and trajectory of Britain's counter-terrorism operations. Palestine Action had targeted Israeli companies and institutions operating in the country before facing legal restrictions. The timing suggests a potential shift in how authorities applied counter-terrorism powers in relation to activism around Palestinian issues.

title: Half of UK terror arrests since 9/11 came after Palestine Action ban
